arxiv-2002-01575.title: Seeing through the smoke : a world-wide comparative study of e-cigarette flavors, brands and markets using data from reddit and twitter
arxiv-2002-01575.creator: Rohit Venkata Sai Dulam, Meghana Murthy, Jiebo Luo, rdulam@ur.rochester.edu, mmurthy@ur.rochester.edu, jluo@cs.rochester.edu
arxiv-2002-01575.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Rohit Venkata Sai Dulam, Meghana Murthy, Jiebo Luo, rdulam@ur.rochester.edu, mmurthy@ur.rochester.edu, jluo@cs.rochester.edu. The growing popularity of E-cigarettes, an alternative to cigarettes, have motivated us to study trends pertaining to the brands, flavors and online market activity using posts from Reddit and Twitter. The main motivation for this world-wide study is to emphasize the difference that laws and regulations have on the usage and availability of different flavors and brands of vapes in different countries.

arxiv-2012-05068.title: A new model of regular black hole in ( 2 + 1 ) (2+1) dimensions
arxiv-2012-05068.creator: Milko Estrada, Francisco Tello-Ortiz
arxiv-2012-05068.description: Abstract We provide a new regular black hole solution in ( 2 + 1 ) (2+1) dimensions with presence of matter fields in the energy momentum tensor. The inclusion of our proposed energy density plus a negative cosmological constant allows that the solution can have both flat as de–Sitter or Anti de–Sitter core.

arxiv-2104-04162.title: eGAN: Unsupervised approach to class imbalance using transfer learning
arxiv-2104-04162.creator: Ademola Okerinde, Tom Theis, Nasik Nafi, William Hsu, Lior Shamir
arxiv-2104-04162.description: Abstract Class imbalance is an inherent problem in many machine learning classification tasks. This often leads to learned models that are unusable for any practical purpose. In this study, we explore an unsupervised approach to address class imbalance by leveraging transfer learning from pre-trained image classification models.

arxiv-2107-07586.title: Photon radiation effects in kinematic reconstruction of top quarks
arxiv-2107-07586.creator: and K. Skovpen
arxiv-2107-07586.description: Abstract Kinematic reconstruction of top quarks allows to define a set of kinematic observables relevant to various physics processes that involve top quarks and provides an additional handle for the suppression of background events. Radiation of photons in association with the top quarks alters the kinematics and the topology of the event, leading to visible systematic effects in measurable observables.

arxiv-2201-01439.title: Construction of extremal Type II ℤ 2 ​ k \mathbb{Z}_{2k} -codes
arxiv-2201-01439.creator: Masaaki Harada
arxiv-2201-01439.description: Abstract We give methods for constructing many self-dual ℤ m \mathbb{Z}_{m} -codes and Type II ℤ 2 ​ k \mathbb{Z}_{2k} -codes of length 2 ​ n 2n starting from a given self-dual ℤ m \mathbb{Z}_{m} -code and Type II ℤ 2 ​ k \mathbb{Z}_{2k} -code of length 2 ​ n 2n , respectively.

arxiv-2201-06045.title: CISRNet: Compressed Image Super-Resolution Network
arxiv-2201-06045.creator: Agus Gunawan, Sultan Rizky Hikmawan Madjid {agusgun, suulkyy}@kaist.ac.kr
arxiv-2201-06045.description: Abstract In recent years, tons of research has been conducted on Single Image Super-Resolution (SISR). However, to the best of our knowledge, few of these studies are mainly focused on compressed images. A problem such as complicated compression artifacts hinders the advance of this study in spite of its high practical values.

arxiv-2204-01081.title: Faces: AI Blitz XIII Solutions
arxiv-2204-01081.creator: Andrew Melnik, Eren Akbulut, Jannik Sheikh, Kira Loos, Michael Büttner, Tobias Lenze
arxiv-2204-01081.description: Abstract AI Blitz XIII Faces challenge hosted on www.aicrowd.com platform consisted of five problems: Sentiment Classification, Age Prediction, Mask Prediction, Face Recognition, and Face De-Blurring. Our team GLaDOS took second place. Here we present our solutions and results. Code implementation: https://github.com/ndrwmlnk/ai-blitz-xiii 1 Sentiment Classification: Classify Facial Expressions 1.

arxiv-2312-07803.title: Feasible Space Monitoring for Multiple Control Barrier Functions with application to Large Scale Indoor Navigation
arxiv-2312-07803.creator: Hardik Parwana, Mitchell Black, Bardh Hoxha, Hideki Okamoto, Georgios Fainekos, Danil Prokhorov, Dimitra Panagou
arxiv-2312-07803.description: Abstract Quadratic programs (QP) subject to multiple time-dependent control barrier function (CBF) based constraints have been used to design safety-critical controllers. However, ensuring the existence of a solution at all times to the QP subject to multiple CBF constraints (hereby called compatibility) is non-trivial.

The dataset was recorded using FAST’s L L -band 19-beam receiver and covered ∼ 3.

arxiv-2601-22515.title: Jingtong Dou
arxiv-2601-22515.description: Abstract As generative AI achieves hyper-realism, superficial artifact detection has become obsolete. While prevailing methods rely on resource-intensive fine-tuning of black-box backbones, we propose that forgery detection capability is already encoded within pre-trained models rather than requiring end-to-end retraining. To elicit this intrinsic capability, we propose the discriminative neural anchors (DNA) framework, which employs a coarse-to-fine excavation mechanism.

pmc-10535249.title: Identification of Acid Hydrolysis Metabolites of the Pimelea Toxin Simplexin for Targeted UPLC-MS/MS Analysis
pmc-10535249.creator: Zhi Hung Loh, Natasha L Hungerford, Diane Ouwerkerk, Athol V Klieve, Mary T Fletcher
pmc-10535249.description: Pimelea poisoning of cattle is a unique Australian toxic condition caused by the daphnane orthoester simplexin present in native Pimelea pasture plants. Rumen microorganisms have been proposed to metabolise simplexin by enzymatic reactions, likely at the orthoester and epoxide moieties of simplexin, but a metabolic pathway has not been confirmed.

pmc-10614681.title: Photocurable injectable Janus hydrogel with minimally invasive delivery for all-in-one treatment of gastric perforations and postoperative adhesions
pmc-10614681.creator: Xiaoqi Wu, Zihan Wang, Jie Xu, Liu Yu, Maoyu Qin, Jianfeng Li, Sitian Liu, Weihan Zheng, Zeyu Li, Jun Ouyang, Yanbing Li, Guoxin Li, Ling Wang, Wenhua Huang, Yaobin Wu
pmc-10614681.description: Background: Surgical sutures for sealing gastric perforations (GP) are associated with severe inflammation and postoperative adhesions. Hydrogel bioadhesives offer a potential alternative for sutureless repair of GP; however, their application in minimally invasive surgery is limited due to their prefabricated patch-form, lacking in situ gelation capability.

pmc-11465556.title: Effect of Leaving Centrosymmetric Character on Spectral Properties in Mono-, Bi-, and Triphotonic Absorption Spectroscopies
pmc-11465556.creator: Ricard Gelabert, Miquel Moreno, José M Lluch
pmc-11465556.description: Numerical simulations of the absorption bands of photoswitch E-o-tetrafluoroazobenzene in DMSO solution under one-, two-, and three-photon absorption conditions combined with the analysis of the behavior of transition probability under distortion of planarity reveal many similarities between the mono- and triphoton spectroscopic behaviors with a two-photon spectrum being set apart.

pmc-11503384.title: Dementia Rehabilitation Training for General Practitioners and Practice Nurses: Does It Make a Difference?
pmc-11503384.creator: Den-Ching A Lee, Grant Russell, Terry P Haines, Keith D Hill, Claire M C O’Connor, Natasha Layton, Kate Swaffer, Marita Long, Catherine Devanny, Michele L Callisaya, Brendan McCormack
pmc-11503384.description: Background/Objectives: Rehabilitation helps reduce disability in dementia. The Australian National Dementia Action Plan identifies a gap in clear treatment pathways post-diagnosis, affecting the quality of life for those with dementia. This study assessed the impact of a one-day dementia training course and follow-up on GPs’ and practice nurses’ knowledge, attitudes, and confidence regarding dementia rehabilitation.

The abundance of environmental A.

pmc-12577124.title: Isolation and characterisation of AFP+/DLK1+ double-positive hepatic stem/progenitor-like cells from fibrotic partial hepatectomy model
pmc-12577124.creator: Shuangliang Sun, Tegshjargal Badamjav, Namur Narid, Urjims Xu, Dunfu Suo, Batbold Batsaikhan, Bayar Hexig
pmc-12577124.description: BackgroundThe liver is an organ with a strong regenerative capacity. Currently, partial hepatectomy (PHx) remains the most effective treatment option within various therapeutic strategies for liver diseases. When the liver undergoes acute injury, such as PHx, the remaining hepatocytes become hypertrophic, re-enter the cell cycle, initiate proliferation, and restore liver function.

pmc-13065569.title: Melatonin effects on the left ventricular function in neonates with persistent pulmonary hypertension
pmc-13065569.creator: Sarah M Nofal, Abdel-Rahman M El-Mashad, Asmaa M Elmesiry, Amany M Abouelenain, Mostafa M Awny
pmc-13065569.description: The aim of this study is to investigate the effects of melatonin on the left ventricular (LV) function in persistent pulmonary hypertension of the newborn (PPHN) and to assess its potential role in enhancing cardiac performance and reducing oxidative stress. This randomized controlled trial was conducted on 80 neonates (≥ 36 weeks’ gestational age) with PPHN confirmed by echocardiography (Echo).

pmc-13242339.title: Modifying the Meaning of the Upper Anchor Predictably Shapes Ratings of Perceived Effort: A Randomized Crossover Trial
pmc-13242339.creator: Dennis Okhamafe, Yedidya Silverman, Andrew D. Vigotsky, Israel Halperin
pmc-13242339.description: BackgroundRatings of perceived effort (RPE) are used to prescribe and monitor training. Yet, the influence of how the upper anchor (“10”) is defined remains underexplored, despite holding theoretical and practical value. Here, we examined whether modifying the upper anchor predictably modifies RPEs during isometric exercises.MethodsWe conducted a within-subject, randomized crossover study in 26 resistance-trained adults.

pmc-13377484.title: Simple and efficient HPLC-MS/MS method for simultaneous extraction and quantification of anthelmintics in equine manure
pmc-13377484.creator: K Holzer, U Bertsche, M Meyer, T Schilling, J Pfannstiel, LE Hoelzle
pmc-13377484.description: Anthelmintic treatment is a common practice in horses. The presence of pharmaceutical residues in fields and pastures is well-documented affecting various organisms, like nematodes.This study describes the development and validation of a high-performance liquid chromatography tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS/MS) method using multiple reaction monitoring (MRM) for extracting and determining the concentrations of four commonly used anthelmintics in horse manure.

pmc-13396399.title: Structural basis for a filamentous morpheein model of human cystathionine beta-synthase
pmc-13396399.creator: Inayathulla Mohammed, Ela Mijatovic, Thilo Magnus Philipp, Lucia Janickova, Kelly Ascencao, Francisco J Asturias, Luis Alfonso Martinez-Cruz, Csaba Szabo, Henning Stahlberg, Tomas Majtan
pmc-13396399.description: Human cystathionine beta-synthase (CBS) is a vital enzyme that regulates sulfur amino acid metabolism, hydrogen sulfide production, and cellular redox balance. Using a multidisciplinary approach, we demonstrate that CBS functions as a filamentous morpheein, with its stability, turnover, and activity governed by dynamic quaternary structural transitions.

pmc-13617751.title: Hair loss in the era of CGRP inhibition: emerging evidence, mechanisms, and clinical implications
pmc-13617751.creator: Adelė Antanaitytė, Mantas Jokubaitis, Jorinta Jokubaitė, Kristina Ryliškienė
pmc-13617751.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionCalcitonin gene-related peptide (CGRP)-targeting therapies have transformed migraine management and are generally associated with a favorable safety profile. However, accumulating real-world evidence suggests a potential association with alopecia that was not systematically captured in pre-approval clinical trials. This review aimed to synthesize current evidence on alopecia associated with CGRP-targeting therapies, with a focus on clinical patterns, pharmacovigilance signals and underlying pathophysiological mechanisms.MethodsA structured literature search of PubMed was conducted to identify relevant evidence on CGRP-targeting therapies and hair loss through August, 2026.
